title: Gas excitation of post-SB galaxies at 0.6 < z < 1.3
question: What is the physical excitation state of molecular gas in post-starburst galaxies at 0.6 < z < 1.3, and what mechanisms drive their low star formation efficiency?

data.angular_resolution: 0.5'' - 1.4'' (CO 5-4); up to 3.06'' x 2.16'' in archival low-J data
data.sensitivity: Continuum RMS 0.008 - 0.083 mJy/beam (Table 1); 12.6 - 99.3 uJy (260-360 GHz continuum); 4.5 - 21.0 uJy (broad continuum)

what.value: Stellar masses, SFRs, Dn4000, and time since quenching for SQuIGGLE galaxies

evidence.quote: All our targets have available estimates of the D$_n$4000 spectral index, a useful tool to constrain the mean stellar age of galaxies with younger galaxies having on average a less pronounced 4000-break (cite: Bezanson2021; Zanella2023).

what.value: Time since quenching for SQuIGGLE sample

evidence.quote: For the SQuIGG$\vec{L}$E sample (cite: Bezanson2021) and (cite: Suess2021) also published an estimate of the time since quenching derived from the star formation history provided by the `Prospector` stellar population synthesis modeling.

what.value: Stellar masses, SFRs, and Dn4000 for ID83492, ID97148, and companions
Average CO excitation ratios for local post-starbursts (R31 = 0.32, R21 = 0.52, R32 = 0.62)

evidence.quote: We re-estimated the molecular gas masses considering the average excitation factors obtained for local post-SBs, namely $R_{31} = 0.32$, $R_{21} = 0.52$, and $R_{32} = 0.62$ (cite: French2021).
In these cases, we estimated $L'_\mathrm{CO(2-1)}$ from $L'_\mathrm{CO(3-2)}$ assuming the average ratio $R_{32} = 0.62$ of local post-starbursts (cite: French2023).

what.value: Comparison samples of local and high-redshift main-sequence galaxies, ULIRGs, and starbursts

evidence.quote: as well as comparison samples of local and high-redshift main-sequence galaxies, local Ultra Luminous Infrared Galaxies (ULIRGs), and high-redshift starbursts from the literature (cite: Liu2021).

what.value: CO(5-4) - L_IR scaling relation for star-forming galaxies

evidence.quote: We converted the CO(5-4) luminosity into total IR luminosity ($\mathrm{L_{IR}}$) following the relation of (cite: Valentino2020b)

what.value: Average SED template for quiescent galaxies

evidence.quote: To this end, we used the average SED template for quiescent galaxies from (cite: Magdis2021), which is characterized by a dust temperature $T_\mathrm{d} = 20\, \mathrm{K}$

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw ALMA visibilities and convert to uvfits for GILDAS analysis
recipe.method: Standard ALMA calibration pipeline followed by conversion to uvfits format and 3x spectral binning
key_parameters: 3x velocity binning from native 6.5 - 13.5 km s^-1 resolution

recipe.goal: Extract 1D spectra and measure CO(5-4) and archival low-J CO line fluxes and redshifts in the uv plane
recipe.method: Iterative channel-by-channel uv-plane fitting of an elliptical Gaussian at fixed CO(2-1) position to extract 1D spectra, followed by 1D Gaussian fitting on optimal S/N spectrum
key_parameters: 3 sigma detection threshold; 3 sigma upper limits using CO(2-1) channel range for non-detections
assumptions: Elliptical Gaussian source model with fixed aperture across all channels and transitions

recipe.goal: Stack CO(5-4) non-detections in the uv plane
recipe.method: Align individual CO(5-4) maps to CO(2-1) positions, coadd visibilities, and fit stacked uv data with a 2D Gaussian
assumptions: 2D Gaussian parameters fixed to those obtained from the CO(2-1) stack

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum upper limits and search for serendipitous continuum sources
recipe.method: Integrate visibilities over line-free spectral ranges (both 260-360 GHz and combined with lower-J continuum bands)
key_parameters: 3 sigma upper limits for continuum flux

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas masses and excitation ratios (R52, R53) and compute sample averages
recipe.method: Calculate brightness temperature luminosity ratios R52 and R53, convert low-J CO to M_H2, and compute sample mean R52 using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and stacking
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.4 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 for post-SBs and 0.8 for starbursting companions
Excitation ratios R31 = 0.32, R21 = 0.52, R32 = 0.62 for post-SBs; R31 = 0.66, R21 = 0.85, R32 = 0.78 for starbursting companions

recipe.goal: Construct CO SLEDs and compare with theoretical models and test for residual obscured star formation
recipe.method: Normalize CO SLEDs to CO(2-1), compare with Narayanan et al. (2014) models, and compare L_IR predicted from CO(5-4) against maximum L_IR allowed by continuum non-detections
key_parameters: Sigma_SFR = 0.05 to > 500 M_sun yr^-1 kpc^-2 for SLED models; T_d = 20 K and 30 K for dust SED templates
assumptions: Pseudo CO(2-1) derived using R32 = 0.50 in SLED plot for galaxies lacking CO(2-1); Valentino2020b CO(5-4)-L_IR relation; Kennicutt2021 L_IR-SFR relation

answer_key.quantity: Stacked R52 upper limit (Non merging post-SBs)

evidence.quote: Non-detections have on average a tight upper limit $R_{52} < 0.10$ ($1\sigma$) derived by stacking (see Sec. [3.1](#subsec:co54)).

answer_key.quantity: Maximum obscured SFR from dust continuum non-detections (T_d = 20 K)

evidence.quote: This yielded the maximum $\mathrm{L_{IR}}$ allowed by the lack of continuum detection, and maximum obscured $\mathrm{SFRs < 18\, M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$, consistent with values expected for quiescent galaxies.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum obscured SFR from dust continuum non-detections (T_d = 30 K)

evidence.quote: This yielded even lower maximum L$_\mathrm{IR}$ and more stringent $\mathrm{SFR < 11\, M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$.

Exact velocity/frequency channel ranges integrated for each line and excluded for continuum maps
Modified blackbody spectral emissivity index (beta) used when rescaling the Magdis et al. (2021) SED template from 20 K to 30 K

score_reason: All 7 ALMA project codes are explicitly listed and standard pipeline calibration was used without complex custom imaging, since all flux extraction is done in the uv plane with GILDAS uv_fit. However, the exact sizes/orientations of the fixed elliptical Gaussian models and the exact velocity integration windows are not tabulated.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are identified, calibration relies on the standard ALMA pipeline, and the primary results are concrete numeric line fluxes, luminosities, and excitation ratios (R52, R53) tabulated per target.
